headline: Heavy rain and hill torrents leave thousands stranded in Chattogram
summary: Severe flooding in eastern and southern Chattogram has left residents of multiple upazilas trapped in their homes as water levels rise.
details: Heavy rainfall and hill torrents over several days have flooded vast areas of eastern and southern Chattogram, leaving hundreds of thousands of people stranded.
Residents in upazilas including Satkania, Lohagara, Chandanaish, and Banshkhali are facing extreme hardship as floodwaters enter their homes.
Many have been forced to seek shelter on rooftops or higher ground as roads are submerged, cutting off communication with other areas.
The region is currently facing a severe shortage of pure drinking water and dry food, with affected residents awaiting emergency assistance.

headline_marked: Malaysia introduces [[new worker recruitment rules]] to prioritize locals
headline: Malaysia introduces new worker recruitment rules to prioritize locals
summary: Foreign workers will only be hired if local candidates are not found, shifting the focus to the domestic workforce.
details: Malaysia has introduced new regulations for the recruitment of workers, prioritizing local citizens over foreign nationals.
Under the new rules, employers must first seek and seek out local candidates for available positions before they can apply to hire foreign workers.
This policy shift aims to reduce the dependency on foreign labor and strengthen the domestic job market for Malaysian citizens.
The move is expected to impact the recruitment process for various sectors that have traditionally relied heavily on foreign manpower.
Foreign workers will now only be considered as a last resort when suitable local talent is not available to fill the critical roles.
caption:
Malaysia is prioritizing its own citizens for jobs. Foreign workers will now only be hired if no local candidates are found.

Malaysia has introduced new regulations for the recruitment of workers, prioritizing local citizens over foreign nationals.

Under the new rules, employers must first seek and seek out local candidates for available positions before they can apply to hire foreign workers.

This policy shift aims to reduce the dependency on foreign labor and strengthen the domestic job market for Malaysian citizens.

The move is expected to impact the recruitment process for various sectors that have traditionally relied heavily on foreign manpower.

Foreign workers will now only be considered as a last resort when suitable local talent is not available to fill the critical roles.
